tips: Load Suica to Apple/Google Wallet now while on Wi-Fi at MSP — land in Tokyo ready to tap.
Set phones to JST during the MSP layover to start tricking your body clock.
Hit the Limousine Bus ATM at Haneda; your Airbnb likely needs cash.
Jet-lag crash is real — if you hit the wall, grab konbini sustenance and sleep without shame.

2026-12-16.weatherAlert: December evenings in Tokyo are dry but near-freezing (~5°C). The 2-hour outdoor nomihodai at 19:30 will feel much colder than expected.
2026-12-16.crowdAlert: Shibuya Sky sunset slots are notoriously crowded; if you don't have a pre-booked time, expect a long wait or sell-out.

suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Mag's Park rooftop (free–$2 (¥0–300)) or Shibuya Hikarie 11F Sky Lobby (free)
suggestedSwap.reason: Shibuya Sky often sells out for sunset; the free/cheap alternatives offer great crossing views without the queue or cost.

tips: Layer up heavily for the outdoor izakaya — sitting still in December cold drains you fast.
If the crew is wiped, swap the Blue Cave walk for an early nomihodai and call it a night.

2026-12-17.weatherAlert: Typical December rain risk in the afternoon. Ueno Ameyoko and Skytree queues are fully exposed.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Ueno Ameyoko market under the tracks
suggestedSwap.reason: If it rains, the exposed Ameyoko market is miserable; the museum is indoors and perfectly located between Asakusa and Akiba.

tips: Skytree night queues can be brutal — Asahi Beer Hall's 22F Sky Room next door gives the same view for the price of a beer.
Kamiya Bar's Denki Bran is a cheap, historic pre-Skytree warmer.

2026-12-18.crowdAlert: teamLab Planets requires strict adherence to your booked time slot; arriving late risks denied entry.
tips: Do your Ginza Uniqlo flagship shopping now — luggage moves to Kyoto tomorrow.
Golden Gai bars seat 4-6 max; split the 8-person squad into two groups and cross-pollinate.

2026-12-19.weatherAlert: High wind and rain risk for the coastal Enoden tram and Enoshima island climb. Fuji visibility over Sagami Bay is very low in bad weather.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Enoshima island — climb to the Sea Candle
suggestedSwap.reason: If rain hits, the Enoshima climb is slippery and windy with zero Fuji view; Hokokuji offers a covered matcha experience in a quiet bamboo grove.

tips: Check the Fuji visibility forecast in the morning; if it's zero, pivot to the Nikko or Hokokuji alternatives.
The Enoden tram gets packed; try to board at the first stop (Kamakura) to guarantee seats for the group.
Run the Airbnb laundry tonight so everyone lands in Kyoto with clean clothes.
Pack for Kyoto BEFORE the farewell dinner and Golden Gai encore — midnight packing with 8 people is chaos.
Grab ekiben at Tokyo Station's Matsuri store before boarding — the Shinkansen food cart is weak.
Sit on the LEFT side (Seat E) on the Shinkansen for the Mt. Fuji view at ~minute 40.

2026-12-22.weatherAlert: Rain makes the Fushimi Inari stone steps dangerously slippery and the Kiyomizu-dera stage cold and wet.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Kiyomizu-dera — the wooden stage over the valley
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Sanjusangendo — 1,001 golden Kannon statues in a 120m hall
suggestedSwap.reason: If raining, the walk down Sannenzaka to Kiyomizu is treacherous; Sanjusangendo is indoor, jaw-dropping, and nearby.

tips: Funaoka Onsen's electric bath is intense — start on the low setting before committing.
Past Yotsutsuji at Fushimi Inari, the crowds vanish; push 45 more minutes for deserted gates.

2026-12-23.weatherAlert: Rain turns the Arashiyama bamboo grove into a dark, slippery photo-op and makes Nara deer interactions messy.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove before the buses exist
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: SNOW PROTOCOL: Kinkaku-ji at opening (gold + snow = Japan's rarest photo), Fushimi round two after
suggestedSwap.reason: If Kyoto wakes up white (rare but possible in late Dec), the snow protocol overrides everything for the ultimate photo. If rain, the bamboo is gloomy; pivot to indoor Sanjusangendo or Tofuku-ji.

tips: Wakakusa-yama is CLOSED today (closes 2nd Sunday of Dec) — do not attempt the climb.
Bow to the deer first; show empty hands when done. Never run.

2026-12-24.crowdAlert: KFC Christmas buckets sell out fast in Japan; pre-ordering is often required, or you must go early.
tips: Hit the KFC by 17:30 at the latest — Christmas Eve buckets are a national obsession and vanish quickly.
Buy Rikuro's jiggly cheesecake near Namba station; it wobbles and disappears within the hour.

2026-12-25.crowdAlert: USJ on Christmas Day will be at peak capacity. Mario Kart and Forbidden Journey lines will exceed 2 hours without Express Passes.
tips: Rope-drop Super Nintendo World immediately; do not detour.
If Kinopio's Cafe is full, Yoshi's snack stand and Power-Up Band challenges still deliver the serotonin.

2026-12-26.weatherAlert: Miyajima ferry and torii gate views are highly susceptible to fog and rain in December, potentially obscuring the floating effect.
tips: This is the longest day of the trip. If anyone is redlining, they should skip Miyajima, do the museum unhurried, and meet at Hiroshima station.
Shukkei-en garden is a quiet, beautiful walk if the Peace Museum hits too heavy.

2026-12-27.weatherAlert: The Midosuji Illumination walk (4km) is fully exposed to cold December winds.
tips: 551 Horai butaman 4-pack from Namba station BEFORE the crab dinner — they sell out nightly.
Misono Building bars are tiny; send scouts ahead to secure seats for 4 while the others wait.
Check tax-free paperwork tonight: receipts with passports, purchases accessible — customs CAN ask on exit.
Kobe beef budget fork: $22 (¥3,500) bowls and croquettes around Sannomiya deliver 70% of the experience at 40% of the price.
Sit on the LEFT side (Seat A) on the Shinkansen for Mt. Fuji's encore.
Zero out your Suica cards and do final boss gachapon at the gate — leftover Suica cash is hard to refund.

globalTips: With USD/JPY at ~161.65, your dollar stretches far. Withdraw large lump sums at 7-Eleven ATMs to minimize per-transaction fees rather than making daily small withdrawals.
December in Japan is cold, dry, and occasionally rainy. Pack versatile, thin layers (heat-tech) rather than bulky coats, and always carry a compact umbrella for sudden showers.

For a group of 8, always split into two squads of 4 for restaurants, bars, and small spaces. Japanese venues rarely accommodate large groups, and splitting doubles your chances of getting seated immediately.
